slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop wasting
your evenings
Decide your evening before it starts. One plan on the way home: gym, cooking, a call, a book. Evenings without a plan always end in scrolling.
Change clothes as soon as you get home. It tells your brain the workday is over, and you'll feel ready to do something for yourself.
Cook a real dinner. Thirty minutes in the kitchen with music on is relaxing, cheaper and healthier than another delivery. Try it tonight and see.
Leave your phone in another room for an hour. It's amazing how long an evening feels once your phone isn't in your hand. Then read for twenty minutes.
Before: my evenings disappeared into my phone. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I go to bed feeling I used my time.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: my evenings disappeared into my phone. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I go to bed feeling I used my time.

slides.texte_overlay: See people in real life once or twice a week. A walk with a friend or dinner with family beats any evening alone on the couch. Same time, every night.
Wind down the same way every night. Dim lights, a shower, a few pages of a book. A calm routine makes you sleep better and wake up stronger.
